limitations: Static MVP: generated scenarios are candidates; run the function and verify actual branch coverage with Jest/Istanbul.

MC/DC mode uses unique-cause independence: for each atomic condition, a pair must differ only in that condition while the full decision changes. This is static candidate generation; execute and verify the pairs in the target runtime.

JavaScript is supported via the TypeScript parser with allowJs. Without JSDoc, property types are inferred from comparisons, truthiness checks, switch cases, nested accesses and .length; inferredProperties reports confidence and evidence.

Supported conditions: direct parameter paths, literals, truthiness, !, &&, ||, equality, numeric comparisons, and simple numeric comparisons between two input paths. Unknown truthy/falsy properties use boolean representatives unless nested access implies an object/array.
Supported control flow: if/else, switch with literal cases, ternary expressions, for/for...of/for...in/while/do...while loops, plus break/continue path termination inside loops and switch clauses.

Loop scenarios: for...of and for...in generate zero-, one- and multiple-iteration collection shapes; loop-body aliases are mapped to a representative first item. Classic for loops support literal counter initializers and simple increment/decrement steps; while/do...while support simple property constraints and local numeric counter cases.

Loop analysis is an approximation: common break/continue transfers stop analysis of the current path; break inside switch exits the switch, while continue propagates to the enclosing loop. Labelled transfers, full iteration-state propagation and switch fallthrough are not modeled. Mutations to iterated collections, custom iterators, async iterator side effects, and complex counter updates are unsupported.

Array callback support: forEach/map/flatMap/some/every/filter/find/findIndex and reduce with inline callbacks and collections resolved to function input paths. Predicate callbacks support concise expressions and block callbacks with a single return; safe top-level const aliases are expanded before MC/DC analysis. Block callbacks with explicit if decisions also expand safe const aliases in their conditions. For predicates that use the callback index parameter, unique-cause MC/DC searches representative callback indexes 0 and 1 and can emit a cross-index independence pair; pair scenarios carry the actual iterationIndex. Only immutable const declarations with side-effect-free initializers are inlined; let/var, destructuring, reassignment, helper calls, getters and mutation-dependent values are not symbolically expanded. Direct find() checks and find() comparisons with null/undefined are supported, as are findIndex() comparisons against numeric literals. some/every have representative match/no-match scenarios. flatMap chains support a direct array-property projection (for example group => group.passengers). reduce analyzes callback indexes through 2 with an initial value and through 3 without one, replaying up to two prior callback invocations over bounded candidate items. This is concrete interpretation, not general symbolic execution; unsupported reducer statements are not replaced with a fabricated initial accumulator state.
Undefined values are encoded as {"$undefined":true}; omit the corresponding argument/property or hydrate this marker before calling the function.
Mock templates are type-derived suggestions and are not automatically connected to branch scenarios.
